notes: Merged from two passes that agree on every id and value (case 1: source email, group 5, priority high, status work_in_progress; skill 20 'Strategic Onboarding'; user_skill 336 for Casey Green 52; rule 9 on priority high, the skill by name, group 5, active) and on six of seven dispositions. disagreement: granularity: A tests the move, priority and status in one change requirement, B in three; kept B's split because the sentence asks three things (one requirement per thing). disagreement: stay on user_skill (user = 52 AND skill = 2, expected 0) guarding the near-match 'Employee Onboarding' skill (A only); dropped because a stay is only what the request or policy forbids or the boundary of a selector, and neither applies: the skill and its assignment are anchored by id (skill 20 with its name, user_skill 336 with skill = 20), so assigning skill 2 instead fails the creates directly, and assigning it as well is collateral change, measured separately. disagreement: comprehensive_transaction_integrity_check: A kept, B excluded; chose kept, carried jointly (logged in its evidence). The based_on_skills cell is the one addition beyond the benchmark: the request fixes it ('with this skill'), but the stored form (JSON names on the seed) is a convention the tool may not follow. The two existence checks are weak: they test seed facts. The case's assigned_to (Travis Wood, not a member of the new group) is left untested as the request does not mention him.
